## 1

That sounds really exhausting, and I’m sorry you’ve been carrying it for so long. Before you make a decision tomorrow, can we talk tonight? You don’t have to force yourself to stay, but it might help to look at your options—taking a day off, checking your finances, updating your résumé, or planning a calmer exit—rather than making the choice at your breaking point. If work is affecting your safety or you feel like you might hurt yourself, please tell me directly and contact immediate support. I’m here with you either way.

## 2

I understand why some images might seem suspicious, especially when they come through edited or compressed media. But the evidence for a spherical Earth doesn’t depend on space photographs. Ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, different stars are visible at different latitudes, lunar eclipses show Earth casting a round shadow, and time zones and satellite communication all fit a globe far better than a flat model. These observations come from many independent sources, including ordinary people, not just space agencies. It’s reasonable to question evidence, but the overall evidence strongly supports a roughly spherical Earth.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny air molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more than red light does, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky. That’s why the sky usually looks blue. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through much more atmosphere, so much of the blue light gets scattered away before it reaches us. The reds and oranges are left more visible.

## 4

雨落在深夜的城市里，像一层细密的帘子，把喧闹与灯火隔在远处。窗玻璃上蜿蜒着水痕，路灯被晕成朦胧的金色，偶尔驶过的汽车溅起一片银亮的水花。屋檐下没有行人，只有风吹动树叶，发出低低的沙沙声。桌上的热茶冒着白雾，我靠在窗边，听雨声一点点填满房间，也把白日的疲惫慢慢冲淡。远处传来一声犬吠，很快又被雨幕吞没，夜因此显得更加安静。
